beats.headline: A parade float
beats.text: A wall of blue dots comes down the hallway, and Carl laughs: they have built a parade float. Imani and Chris strain at the front in leather pig harnesses from the tuskling courtesans. Wheels from wheelchairs that no longer have owners are fixed to long wooden platforms, cobbled together with goblin tools, the wood from the blimp boss's warehouse. It is more like a train, ten cars of four, most riders in their own chairs locked two by two, the walker users cross-legged on the boards. More maneuverable than it looks, Brandon says, but too wide for a safe room door. He added ramps.

beats.headline: Too wide for the door
beats.text: Jack has stood up on the last car to piss on the wall. Yolanda's arrow kills him and he falls off the trailer, and as the train lurches forward Randall flies off the last car with his walker. A monster forms out of the sizzling stain: a Rage Elemental. The train rockets past Carl toward the safe room a hundred feet away, but its cars are too wide for the entrance, so Imani and Chris pull people off their chairs and toss them through the door. Gravity reverses. The last car flies up and dangles from the ceiling, still chained to the rest, and Mrs. McGibbons slams into the roof of the hallway.

beats.headline: Ash in the hallway
beats.text: Carl pushes hard on the pedals and they rush out into the hallway. Everything out there is blackened and turned to ash, and it smells like burning garbage. There is no sign of the train cars, or of the wheelchairs and walkers that were left behind. The only thing that survived is the long, three-hundred-foot length of glittering magical chain, which Carl grabbed earlier.
